novelty_flags.label: Theorem 6 / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The cited JMLR paper's Jensen relaxation is for its f-divergence base-policy model, whereas the proposal claims a same-normalization comparison while adding an odds cap and using a different full-propensity Pearson cost.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 7
soundness_flags.one_line: After the simultaneous multinomial event, all three asserted containments are immediate from the union definitions of G_n, B_n, and J_n; no nontrivial inferential content or shrinkage result is stated.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 3
soundness_flags.one_line: At Gamma=1 the odds faces force q=e, so the singleton domain and zero cost follow by direct substitution; as a root result it is only a regression/sanity check.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, Proposition 6 and the discussion immediately following it
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves sharp bounds for E[Y(0)] and E[Y(1)] separately and explicitly says simultaneous ATE sharpness may not hold for its average-case model, contrasting Dorn and Guo's worst-case result.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; corroborated by ZhangZhao2026AverageCase Section 3 discussion of Dorn and Guo Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work studies sharp treatment-effect bounds under Tan's marginal sensitivity model; Zhang and Zhao identify its worst-case armwise bounds as simultaneously attainable for the ATE.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 7-10, equations (10)-(16), especially p. 8 equation (12) and p. 9 equation (14)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines an aggregate f-divergence base-policy uncertainty set, relaxes it by Jensen's inequality and conditional-moment constraints, and states that the box constraint has no Jensen relaxation; it does not present the proposal's odds-capped full-law Pearson frontier as that relaxation.
The manuscript studies perturbation of linear SOCP primal and dual problems and establishes Lipschitz continuity and Hadamard directional differentiability of its optimal-value map.

source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economic Studies 86(1), 2019 published version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats inference when a known map is directionally differentiable and supplies derivative-aware resampling when the ordinary bootstrap fails.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1911.10215, revised October 2022 preprint corresponding to JOE 235(2)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops directional-derivative resampling and uniform inference for optimized value-function functionals.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace Theorem 6's attribution with an explicit embedding or non-embedding theorem: define the exact published f-divergence/Jensen program in the proposal's notation, map its budget to R_P if possible, and then prove the rational strict gap; otherwise call J an author-defined relaxation and drop the claimed same-normalization comparison.

Replace Theorem 7's tautological union coverage with a nontrivial result, such as finite-sample outer-diameter control on an explicitly regular interior region, a boundary-rate lower bound, or exact inversion that strictly improves the multinomial union construction.
Move Proposition 3 from a root research target to a regression corollary, or strengthen it to a quantitative Gamma-downarrow-1 stability/boundary result for C_P and I_P.

recommended_next_step: Revise the Jensen-comparator alignment and replace the two definitional root targets with substantive frontier or inference claims; the joint full-law frontier and garbling kernel can then advance to Stage 0 at field tier.
